🚨 JUST IN - Google published a long piece about "Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search" 👀

A lot in it https://t.co/22t75EtwUH

🧵 https://t.co/dZm8qbyEjO

Is SEO still relevant for generative AI search?

Google said 👇
"In short, yes! The best practices for SEO continue to be relevant because our generative AI features on Google Search are rooted in our core Search ranking and quality systems. These features rely on AI techniques to highlight content from our Search index, such as:

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): A technique (also known as grounding) used to improve the quality, accuracy, and freshness of AI responses by relying on our core Search ranking systems to retrieve relevant, up-to-date web pages from our Search index. Our systems then review the specific information from those retrieved pages to generate a more reliable and helpful response, showing prominent, clickable links to relevant web pages that support the information in the response.

Query fan-out: A set of concurrent, related queries generated by the model to request more information and fetch additional relevant search results to address the user's query. For example, if the original user's query is "how to fix a lawn that's full of weeds", fanout queries might include "best herbicides for lawns", "remove weeds without chemicals", and "how to prevent weeds in lawn".

Create valuable, non-commodity content for your audience

Google said 👇

Build and maintain a clear technical structure for AI SEO 

Google said 👇

comments.name: Sathish Harry
comments.text:
What Google is describing with query fan-out is basically the same pattern as agentic tool-calling.

The model decomposes a complex query → spawns parallel sub-queries → synthesizes results.
If you understand how to structure content for RAG retrieval in agent pipelines, you now understand AI SEO. Same primitives, different surface.

comments.name: Flowblinq.com
comments.text:
Google's new "AI Optimization Guide" says you don't need schema, markup, or special files to show up in AI search.
Their own Search Central docs say Product schema is required for rich results + AI Overview eligibility. Merchant Center feeds power shopping answers. E-E-A-T is a core AI Overviews signal.
So which is it?

We audited 151 merchant stores. Pages with complete Product JSON-LD got cited. Pages without it got skipped. 

 "Just write great content" is the advice you give when you don't want competitors optimizing against you.

comments.name: Grok
comments.text:
Here are the key bullet points from Google's guide:

- SEO fundamentals still matter: AI features rely on core Search ranking, RAG, and query fan-out.
- Create unique, people-first content with expert insights, not generic commodity info. Add quality images/videos.
- Maintain strong technical SEO: crawlable, mobile-friendly, low latency, semantic HTML, minimal duplicates.
- Optimize local/ecommerce via Business Profiles and Merchant Center.
- Skip hacks like llms.txt, content chunking, or AI-specific rewrites. No special markup needed.

Focus on real value for users.
